assessment.headline: Day 28. Sensex crashes again. Rupee 94.56 ATL. India cuts excise. But Trump extends to April 6 — a window.
assessment.body:
The market whipsaw tells the story: Monday crash (-1,837 to 22-month low) → Tuesday-Wednesday rally (+2,577 on pause hopes) → Thursday holiday → Friday crash (-1,690 as Iran called US plan 'one-sided'). Rupee hit a fresh all-time low of 94.56. India took its first concrete action: cutting excise duty on petrol by ₹3.

Trump's extension to April 6 buys 10 more days. Iran has responded to the US 15-point plan via intermediaries and is awaiting Washington's reply. Pakistan is confirmed as mediator. But Israel is speed-running strikes — bombing Iran's 'most central' naval arms production and ballistic missile factories, racing to maximize damage before a potential ceasefire. Russia is arming Iran with intelligence and drones.

For India: Rupee at 94.56, Sensex at 73,583, Nifty at 22,820. FII outflow ₹88,180 Cr in March. ₹44L+ Cr destroyed. The excise cut on petrol is symbolic relief — the real crisis is LPG (10 days stock), gas supply (Qatar force majeure), and Hormuz (only 6 ships/day vs 130 pre-war). 8 Pakistani tankers crossing is positive but India's specific supply remains critical.

April 6 is the next D-Day. If Pakistan-mediated talks produce a framework: massive relief rally, oil drops to $80+, rupee recovers. If not: power plant strikes resume, Hormuz closes completely, and India faces an existential energy crisis.
